newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian parliament in uproar over WTO meeting.
newsitem.headline: Indian parliament in uproar over WTO meeting.

text.p: Irate lawmakers demanding a government statement on India's stance at world trade talks forced the abrupt adjournment of both houses of India's parliament on Friday.

Members hit out at Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition, saying the government had caved in under Western pressure over the sensitive issue of labour standards at the meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore.

The speaker of the lower house, P.A. Sangma, demanded that the government provide full details of negotiations over labour standards and investment before India signed the WTO declaration in Singapore. Newspapers said India had softened its stance at the Singapore meeting.
"Things have changed and things are changing," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Sangma as saying.

"We have surrendered to U.S. pressure at the cost of our sovereignty," PTI quoted Rupchand Pal of the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) as saying. The CPI-M supports Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition but is not in the government.

PTI quoted Finance Minister P. Chidambaram as saying the "situation (in Singapore) is evolving", but that "members will be fully satisfied that the position taken by India is fully consistent with its stated position".
